title: Deployment appointment grid and signoff notebook — Oct 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is the working "signoff notebook" and deploy appointment grid for the feature wave planned for 2026-10-20 (UTC rollout lane). The doc focuses on: appointment-style schedule (fixed owner time slots), role-level signoffs, minimal smoke/telemetry checks, and an annotated draft of release notes and known issues. Use as the day-of source-of-truth; copy into the binder and pin to #release-ops.

High-level goals:
- Turn multi-team rollouts into time-boxed appointments (reduces noisy churn).
- Produce deterministic signoffs so canary advances only when signals are green.
- Capture release notes and customer-facing messaging in situ to avoid last-minute gaps.

Quick notes / constraints:
- Scope: hosted API routing update (model variant fallback) + batching tweak for small requests.
- Traffic ramp plan: 0 -> 5% (canary) -> 25% -> 100% over ~8 hours, with manual gates at 5% and 25%.
- Primary region: us-west1. Secondary (fallback): eu-west1.
- Hotfix window reserved 2026-10-21 00:00–06:00 UTC.

Deployment appointment grid (UTC time slots) — owners and goals:
- 08:00–08:30 UTC — Preflight & infra warmup (Owner: Samir Rao)
  - Validate capacity pool, node health, all infra-prometheus exporters up.
  - Run quick GPU health script: /ops/scripts/gpu-health-check.sh
  - Confirm SLO dashboards loaded (console: /dash/latency-overview)

- 08:30–09:00 UTC — Canary deploy (5%) (Owner: Priya Sharma)
  - Promote model-routing feature flag to canary pool.
  - Validate canary nodes have the correct binary (build tag: rw-deploy-2026.10.20-rc1).
  - Smoke: single-shot inference on canary with short prompt set (smoke-prompts/canary-quick.txt).

- 09:00–10:00 UTC — Canary observe & probe (Owner: Elena Gomez)
  - Run telemetry queries (see Telemetry queries section).
  - Watch error budget, tail latency (p95/p99), and request failures.
  - If any red signal: rollback canary (see Rollback matrix).

- 10:00–11:00 UTC — Expand to 25% (Owner: Marcus Patel)
  - Manual approval required from Product and SRE (signoff matrix below).
  - Gradual ramp in three steps: 10% -> 18% -> 25% (10m waits between increases).

- 11:00–12:00 UTC — Stabilize and run extended smoke (Owner: Avery Lin)
  - Run end-to-end tests (E2E suite id: RW-E2E/2026-10-quick) against sample customer flows.
  - Verify billing/cost telemetry and token accounting for new batching setting.

- 12:00–16:00 UTC — Full rollout to 100% (Owner: Release Lead on call)
  - Continue to watch telemetry, be prepared to pause at any manual gate.
  - Start post-rollout sampling for quality regression (see Quality sampling).

Preflight checklist (must be green before 08:00 UTC):
- [ ] All release artifacts built and uploaded (artifact registry tag: rw/2026-10-20-rc1)
- [ ] Smoke prompts and test harness uploaded to artifact bucket
- [ ] DB migrations: none for this deploy (confirm no schema changes)
- [ ] Canary pool has capacity for 5% plus 20% headroom
- [ ] Playbook pinned in slack #release-ops and triage channel created
- [ ] On-call rota published for 08:00–20:00 UTC

Signoff matrix (explicit approvals required at gates) — add timestamp on signoffs:
- Preflight green -> Infra (Samir)
- Canary 5% -> SRE (Elena) + Product (Priya)
- Expand to 25% -> SRE (Elena) + Release Lead (Avery) + Observability (Marcus)
- Full rollout -> Release Lead (Avery) + Eng Director (Jordan Blake)

Telemetry queries (copy these into Datadog/Prometheus on-call view):
- Request failure rate (all clusters): query: sum(rate(api.req_failed[1m])) / sum(rate(api.req_total[1m]))
  - Alert threshold: >0.75% sustained for 10m
- Tail latency: p99 latency per route: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(api.latency_bucket[5m]))
  - Alert threshold: p99 > 1.5s for text-gen routes, p99 > 200ms for embeddings routes
- Token emission anomaly: compare tokens/min to baseline (last 7d) — > +30% deviation triggers investigation
- KV cache hit rate (serving): prefer > 65% for small prompt workloads during canary
- Model mismatch errors: count(model.variant_mismatch) — any >0 needs immediate attention

Signal thresholds (actions):
- Green: all critical alerts silent, p99 within threshold, failure rate <=0.2% -> proceed
- Amber: minor degradations (p99 elevated but failures low) -> pause ramp, run targeted smoke, consult model-team
- Red: failure rate >0.75% or steady 2x baseline error counts -> rollback canary and open incident

Rollback matrix (fast paths):
- Canary rollback (5%): revert routing flag to previous variant (rw-routing-v1); take 1–2 minutes to propagate
- 25% rollback: step back to previous traffic split (25% -> 5%), then to 0% if instability persists
- Full rollback: redeploy prior stable tag (rw/2026-10-13-stable) and scale up; notify customers via incident channel

Day-of operator cheat-sheet (short cues):
- If any green-> proceed. If amber-> escalate within 15m. If red-> rollback immediately and page SRE.
- Keep the 'ops-triage' thread focused: 1) current traffic %, 2) primary failing metric, 3) next action
- Assign a note-taker for each slot (add to meeting notes)

Customer & internal comms plan:
- Pre-rollout: short heads-up sent to CS via private channel with tentative start time and scope (owner: Jordan)
- On major pause/rollback: CS + Trust teams get templated message (see draft messages below)
- Post-rollout: Release notes published to product changelog and included in weekly customer digest

Quality sampling & short evals (automated):
- Sampling policy: 2% of successful responses at 25% rollout, 1% at full rollout sent to regression-evals pipeline
- Run lightweight semantic checks: BLEU/ROUGE style similarity + LLM-based hallucination heuristics (pipeline id: RW-qual-2026-10)

Release notes (draft) — keep concise for customers:
- What changed: Model routing now prefers smaller, quantized variants for short prompt requests (reduces latency and unit cost by ~12%). Batching defaults adjusted to favor single-token low-latency paths for tail-sensitive endpoints.
- Why: Reduce p99 latency spikes on short-text workflows while preserving accuracy for long-context requests.
- Rollout plan: staged canary starting 2026-10-20 08:30 UTC, full rollout expected same day if no regressions.
- Known issues: occasional 502 observed when backend cache miss storms occur under synthetic traffic — mitigation: autoscaling + kv-cache prewarm. Customers with strict latency SLAs can pin to routing variant rw-routing-v1.
- Action for customers: None required. Contact support@redwood.ai for concerns or to request variant pinning.

Draft templated messages:
- Pause/rollback internal: "Rolling back model-routing change. Symptoms: elevated p99 and failure rate >0.8%. Rolling to rw/2026-10-13-stable. ETA to restore: ~15m. Pager: @sre-oncall. Update in 10m or on change."
- Customer-facing (short): "We briefly paused a routing update being rolled out today due to elevated error rates for a subset of requests. We reverted to the prior configuration and are monitoring — no action required on your part. Reach out to support@redwood.ai if you observed issues."

Post-deploy retro checklist (first 48h):
- [ ] Collect sample traces for 1h pre and 1h post to compare tail latency
- [ ] Run the full regression eval suite (RW-qual-2026-10-full)
- [ ] Produce a short postmortem if any amber/red gating occurred
- [ ] Update the runbook with any new mitigations or playbook steps that were used

Open questions / parking lot (to resolve before finalizing runbook):
- Should we default the KV cache prewarm to 10% of canary nodes by default? (ops cost vs benefit)
- Do we want an automated rollback policy at the 25% gate if p99 rises >30%? (requires safe kill switch)
- Confirm final wording for the customer-facing note and channel for publishing (CS vs Product marketing).

Appendix: quick references and commands
- Force rollback: /ops/scripts/force-rollback.sh rw/2026-10-13-stable
- Canary flag toggle (k8s): kubectl set env deployment/model-router MODEL_ROUTING=canary --namespace=redwood-canary
- Telemetry quicklinks: console: /dash/latency-overview | traces: /traces/query?service=model-router

Notes to self: avoid over-automation this week — manual gates have helped catch subtle model-quality regressions in prior waves. Keep the appointment-grid cadence tight (30–60m slots) to limit context switching.

---
Document history:
- 2026-10-12: initial sketch (Avery)
- 2026-10-14: added telemetry thresholds and rollback matrix (Elena)
- 2026-10-18: refined customer messaging and signoff matrix (Marcus)

End of draft.
